notes: Child-specific notices (slice 2). The listener check names the child and nothing else; everything specific is said only after the parent presses 1.
West Bengal usage: টিপুন for press, keys as words (এক, দুই, নয়). Bengali verbs carry no gender, so nothing about the child is gendered.
The child's name takes the genitive as -এর joined by a hyphen (রিয়া-এর) so any name works without inflecting it; a native reviewer should say whether -র after a vowel-ending name sounds better.
Short clips do not open with ধন্যবাদ (the recogniser took it for Hindi on a short clip), so thanks go last in the confirmations.
A1, A3 and A4 share one wording on purpose, and none states a concern.
